data.name: Fard
data.long_meaning: A person who carries or supports something. In Islamic context, it can refer to a supporter of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) or a righteous person who upholds the teachings of Islam.
data.spiritual_meaning: A righteous carrier of the message of Islam.
data.numerology_meaning: Individuals with this name tend to be creative, communicative, and sensitive. They may have a strong desire to be of service to others.

in_arabic.name: فرد
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مفرد يعني الشخص الواحد أو الفرد من الجماعة
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم الفرد مشتق من الفردية، و يعني الشخص الواحد أو الفرد من الجماعة. ورد في القرآن الكريم في عدة مواضع، منها قوله تعالى: 'وَمَا مِنَ الْفَضْلِ إِلَّا مِنَ اللَّهِ' (النساء: 113)، وقد وردت الفردية في سياق الحديث عن توحيد الله وفرادته في الخلق والملك.

in_urdu.name: فرد
in_urdu.meaning: فرد کا مطلب ہے اکیلا شخص یا گروہ سے منفرد
in_urdu.long_meaning: فرد نام کی اصطلاح عربی زبان سے لی گئی ہے، جہاں اس کا مطلب ہے اکیلا شخص یا گروہ سے منفرد۔ اس نام کا تعلق توحید اور یکتاپرستی کے مفاہم سے ہے، جو اسلام کی بنیادی تعلیمات میں شامل ہیں۔ جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں کے ثقافتی سیاق میں، فرد نام اچھے اخلاق اور انفرادیت کی علامت کے طور پر دیکھا جاتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: फर्द
in_hindi.meaning: फर्द का अर्थ है अकेला व्यक्ति या समूह से अलग
in_hindi.long_meaning: फर्द नाम की उत्पत्ति संस्कृत और अरबी भाषाओं में हुई है, जहां इसका अर्थ है अकेला व्यक्ति या समूह से अलग। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, फर्द नाम को एक अच्छा और विशिष्ट अर्थ देने के रूप में देखा जाता है, जो व्यक्ति की अनोखापन और व्यक्तिगतता को दर्शाता है। इस्लामी परंपरा में, फर्द नाम का संबंध अल्लाह की एकता और अद्वितीयता से है।

in_pashto.name: فرد
in_pashto.meaning: فرد معنی دے واحد شخص یا له ډلې څخه جلا
in_pashto.long_meaning: فرد نوم د عربي ژبې څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چیرته چې د واحد شخص یا له ډلې څخه جلا معنی لري. په پښتنو او افغانانو کې، فرد نوم د ښه سلوک او انفراديت د نښې په توګه ليدل کیږي. د اسلامي دود په توګه، فرد نوم د الله تعالی د يوالي او ځانګړيتوب سره تړاو لري.

data.cultural_impact: The term "Fard" is used extensively in the Islamic world, particularly in reference to the Fard Ain, which means the compulsory observances in Islam. These observances include the Five Pillars of Islam: the declaration of faith, prayer, giving to charity, fasting during Ramadan, and the pilgrimage to Mecca. Being a Fard means that these practices are not optional, but required for every Muslim. By following these practices, a Muslim becomes a valued member of the Islamic ummah (community).
data.spiritual_significance: In a deeper spiritual sense, being a Fard also means carrying the responsibility of representing Islam to the world. Muslims are expected to be role models of Islamic values, embodying compassion, forgiveness, and righteousness. By upholding these practices, a Muslim not only fulfills their personal religious obligations but also contributes to the greater good of the Islamic community and humanity as a whole. This spiritual significance reminds us that the actions we take as Muslims have far-reaching impacts and consequences, and we must strive to make the world a better place for all.

historical_references.reference: The Islamic term 'Fard' refers to an obligatory religious duty in Islam, which must be performed by every Muslim. One of the earliest references to Fard in Islamic history is related to the payment of Zakat (alms-giving) which is a compulsory religious tax, one of the Five Pillars of Islam. This practice is rooted in the life of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and was established during the early Islamic community in Medina, around 624 AD.
historical_references.context: Payment of Zakat (alms-giving) as a Fard (obligatory religious duty)

historical_references.reference: Another historical reference to the term 'Fard' in Islam can be found in the context of the Islamic military campaigns (Ghazwa). In this context, Fard means a religious obligation for able-bodied Muslims to participate in military campaigns led by the Islamic state for the defense of the faith and the protection of the Muslim community. This practice was established during the time of the Rightly-Guided Caliphs (Rashidun Caliphate), around 632-661 AD.
historical_references.context: Participation in military campaigns as a Fard (religious obligation)

modern_usage.modern_context: The term 'Fard' in Islam refers to an obligatory act or duty that every Muslim is required to perform. In today's digital age, the concept of Fard has expanded beyond traditional religious practices and is increasingly seen in the context of Islamic finance, community engagement, and charitable giving. Muslims are turning to mobile applications like Meeza, Al Baraka, and Waqfeye to manage their finances in accordance with Islamic law. Online marketplaces such as Souq.com and Zawya.com provide a platform for Muslims to shop ethically and support businesses that adhere to Islamic principles. Digital wallets like PayTm and Snapchat's Snapcash are also popular among Muslims, offering a convenient and secure way to make transactions while maintaining compliance with Islamic financial guidelines.
